x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
Shaedon Sharpe is out 6 months with a torn right meniscus.

Surgery was successful — but the 23-year-old (20.8 PPG last season) is done before camp even opens. Return window: late Feb/early March 2027. #RipCity

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Portland loses Shaedon Sharpe for 6 months — but still has Morant, Lillard, and Holiday in the backcourt.

The Blazers aren't dead. They're just a lot thinner at wing. Six months is a long road back. #RipCity

facebook.long_form:
Window: 9:00 AM ET

Shaedon Sharpe is done before the 2026-27 season even begins.

The Portland Trail Blazers guard tore the lateral meniscus in his right knee during an offseason workout, and while his surgery was successful, he's expected to miss roughly six months. That means the 23-year-old — who averaged 20.8 points per game last season — likely won't return until late February or early March 2027.

The silver lining? Portland's backcourt doesn't fall apart without him. The Blazers still have Ja Morant, Damian Lillard, and Jrue Holiday to lean on. That's a lot of veteran firepower to absorb the blow.

But Sharpe was supposed to be part of the Blazers' next wave — a 20-point scorer at 23 years old is rare. Losing 59 games before the season starts is a real setback, and it could affect his development, his trade value, and how Portland builds around him long-term.

#RipCity | Follow Hoop Heroes for the latest NBA news.

Twelve days. That's how long Stephen Curry has to decide his future in Golden State — at least officially.

Sept. 28 is Warriors media day, and it's also the deadline for Curry and the Warriors to finalize a contract extension. He's eligible for up to 2 years and $136.7 million. His current deal pays him $62.6 million in 2026-27, making him the highest-paid player in the league.

Here's what we know: ESPN confirmed that both Curry and the Warriors have "mutual desire" to keep him in a Golden State uniform for the rest of his career. The Warriors are reportedly letting Curry decide the structure — one year, two years, whatever he wants.

Here's what we don't know: whether the deal gets done by the deadline or if camp opens without a signed extension.

Training camp starts Sept. 29. Twelve days. The clock is running.

stories.title: DOJ Clippers Probe — Federal Investigation Stays Quiet at 14 Days

x_posts.label: Post 3-1
x_posts.text:
The DOJ's criminal probe into the Clippers is still in "earliest stages."

One subpoena issued. No charges filed. The NBA already dropped the hammer: 5 picks, $30M, Ballmer suspended. The feds are a separate matter. #Clippers

x_posts.label: Post 3-2
x_posts.text:
Clippers scandal in 4 lines:
• NBA: 5 picks stripped, $30M fine, Ballmer 1-yr ban
• DOJ (EDNY): Criminal inquiry, "earliest stages"
• Kawhi: $700K fine, now with Toronto
• No charges yet. #Clippers #NBA

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

The FBI and DOJ aren't done with the Los Angeles Clippers.

Even after the NBA issued some of the harshest penalties in league history — five stripped first-round picks, a $30 million fine, and a one-year suspension for owner Steve Ballmer — federal prosecutors in Brooklyn (EDNY) are running their own criminal inquiry into the Clippers' dealings with Kawhi Leonard.

The allegation: the Clippers arranged no-show endorsement deals with four companies that paid Leonard roughly $18 million above what his NBA contract allowed.

Where things stand today: the DOJ investigation remains in "earliest stages." At least one subpoena has been issued. No charges have been filed. Kawhi Leonard was fined $700,000 by the NBA and his trade to Toronto has been ratified. Leonard is no longer a Clipper.

The key context: a criminal investigation is not an indictment. Not all inquiries result in charges. But when the feds are involved in a professional sports scandal, the story doesn't end when the league hands down its punishment.

stories.title: Duren Stalemate — Oct. 1 QO Deadline Is 15 Days Away

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
The Duren standoff: 15 days to Oct. 1.

Pistons offer: $190M/5yr. Duren wants $200M+. Gap: ~$10M. Detroit won't budge.

Sign the $9.6M QO and the Pistons lose matching rights next summer. High stakes. #DetroitBasketball

facebook.long_form:
Window: 1:00 PM ET

Fifteen days until the most awkward moment in Detroit Pistons basketball.

October 1 is the qualifying offer deadline for Jalen Duren — and the 22-year-old center has reportedly been seriously considering signing the $9.6 million QO rather than accepting the Pistons' extension offer of approximately $190 million over five years.

The gap: Detroit is offering around $38 million per year. Duren wants $40 million-plus. The Pistons have reportedly told agents they won't raise their offer.

The math for Duren: take the QO, play out 2026-27, become an unrestricted free agent next summer — and Detroit loses its right to match outside offers. That's the nuclear option for both sides. One year, $9.6 million, and then full freedom.

Detroit has the ability to push the hard deadline as late as March 1, 2027, but at this point, insiders say the team won't budge on money.

Fifteen days to decide.

#DetroitBasketball | Follow Hoop Heroes for all the latest.

The first look at Philadelphia's superteam — and it's already got people talking.

Bleacher Report dropped a workout video of LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, and Tyrese Maxey's first session together with trainer Chris Johnson, and the clips show a level of early chemistry that has 76ers fans buzzing ahead of training camp.

They're running pick-and-rolls, cutting through half-court sets, and finishing at the rim. Nobody looks out of place. Nobody looks like they're figuring out a new system. They look like a team that's been waiting to play together.

Camp opens Sept. 29 — just 13 days away. The first preseason game is Oct. 8 at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn against the Nets (7:30 PM ET). The regular-season opener? Oct. 20 at Madison Square Garden against the defending champion Knicks.

The Sixers haven't won a title since 1983. This might be the closest they've come.
